name: Hercules
hook: Twelve labors, a three-headed dog and the Strait of Gibraltar: the Hercules clues.

facts.label: Hera
facts.statement: Hercules' name means "the glory of Hera," the goddess who persecuted him and helped devise his twelve labors.

facts.label: the Twelve Labors
facts.statement: Hercules performed twelve labors to atone for killing his family, beginning with the Nemean lion and the Hydra.

facts.label: the Nemean lion and Hydra
facts.statement: His first labors were slaying the Nemean lion and the many-headed Hydra of Lerna.

facts.label: Cerberus
facts.statement: His 12th and most dangerous labor was dragging Cerberus, the three-headed dog, up from Hades.

facts.label: the Augean stables
facts.statement: Hercules cleaned King Augeas' vast, filthy stables as one of his labors.

facts.label: Hippolyta's girdle and the golden apples
facts.statement: The two labors that did not involve animals were taking Queen Hippolyta's girdle and fetching the golden apples of the Hesperides.

facts.label: the Pillars of Hercules
facts.statement: The Pillars of Hercules are the two promontories flanking the Strait of Gibraltar, the gateway between the Mediterranean and Atlantic.
